# NW-LYT#2: resource helpers, original instruction reconstruction.
# verify: -calleesp
# Stack objects start with address-periodic bytes on both sides, so a stack byte the original writes and a
# candidate leaves alone (or the reverse) shows up in the objects passed to callees.
stackfill periodic

field 02873B68 56000008 u32 31
# The query name gets its own storage: a name placed over the archive object (e.g. this = NULL and a small r4)
# writes text into the record count; a count of 2^30 or more makes the original's signed midpoint overflow and
# its binary search never ends (both sides hit the access budget, nothing is compared). attach (02873880) takes the
# count from the 16-bit node count of the hash block and rejects counts above 0x3FFF; the name never lives inside
# the archive object. The archive object itself stays unpinned (NULL and random this included).
arg! 02873B68 r4 0x56070000
fieldstr 02873B68 r4 32 "","A","texture"
fieldstr 02873B68 56000300 64 "","A","texture"

# Signalling NaNs in the words these functions copy as floats. The recompiled reference keeps a signalling NaN
# bit-exact when the lfs is followed by its stfs with no other memory access in between (alignTextOrigin, copyFrom,
# the size copy of createFromResource) and quiets it otherwise; the candidates follow that per site
# (verify with -strictnan to compare the payloads; the default tolerates NaN payloads of aligned float words).
